title: A living sacrifice (Romans 12:1–2)
hook: offer your bodies; be transformed by the renewing of your mind

segments.voice: Yesterday, the olive tree, and wild branches grafted in against nature. Your line was you don't support the root. Did you thank someone who carried something good to you? Day three hundred twenty-six.

Sacrifice. The word can bring up something dead: an animal on an altar, smoke going up. Or something given up: the sacrifice fly in baseball, the parent who works two jobs. Something lost so something else can happen. Now put two words together that don't seem to belong: a living sacrifice. For eleven chapters, Paul has been talking about what God has done: grace, faith, the Spirit, nothing can separate us. Now he turns a corner. A small word in his first sentence ties what God has done to how to live. And then he asks for something strange.
screen: `SACRIFICE: SOMETHING DEAD, OR LOST.` → `ELEVEN CHAPTERS OF WHAT GOD HAS DONE.` → `NOW PAUL TURNS A CORNER.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service." Start with therefore. Everything Paul asks from here on grows out of the mercies of God he's already described. Not do this so God will love you, but God has loved you, therefore. Then bodies. Not just your soul, not just your Sunday. Your hands, your feet, your tired back, your Tuesday afternoon. And a living sacrifice. Not killed on an altar, but offered and still breathing, going on with ordinary life as a gift. The King James says reasonable service; the Greek can mean the worship that makes sense, or spiritual worship. Translators still argue about it. Then verse two: "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind." Conformed: pressed into a shape, like dough in a mold. Transformed is a different kind of change. The Greek word is metamorphousthe. You can hear metamorphosis in it: a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. And it's the same word the Gospels use for Jesus on the mountain, when he was transfigured and shone. Notice it's in the passive: be transformed. Christians hear that as something God does, not something a person pulls off by effort. And notice where Paul says the change starts: the renewing of your mind, in what a person thinks about and dwells on. In the letter, these two verses open the practical chapters that follow: worship that walks out of church on two feet.
screen: `THEREFORE: BECAUSE OF GOD'S MERCIES.` · `YOUR BODY, YOUR TUESDAY.` · `CONFORMED, OR TRANSFORMED.` · `METAMORPHOSIS: THE TRANSFIGURATION WORD.` · then, large: `BE YE TRANSFORMED BY THE RENEWING OF YOUR MIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: offer your day as a gift. Settle, and breathe. Picture the rest of your day, hour by hour. The commute, the meetings, the dishes, the kids, the errands. Nothing special. Then imagine holding it all out in open hands, as a gift. Not a performance. Just this ordinary day, offered. Feel your body: your feet on the floor, your hands. These are part of the offering too. If you pray, you can offer the day to God in your own words, or in silence. The bell holds the time.
A living sacrifice. Not something killed on an altar, but a whole ordinary life, body and all, offered as a gift, and transformed.
Your line: be transformed. Today, notice one thing you let into your mind that squeezes you into a shape you don't want, and swap it for one that renews. Day three hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Some Christians begin the day by offering it to God, and some traditions, such as the Catholic Morning Offering, have set prayers for this; Romans 12:1–2 is often memorized.

fork.setup: you're Paul. you've spent eleven chapters on what God has done. how do you begin telling people how to live?
options: with a list of rules to earn God's favor.

fork.reveal: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice." the ethics grow out of the grace.

original.note: Greek: be transformed. the root of metamorphosis, and the word for Jesus's transfiguration.

trapdoor: what you thought: a sacrifice is something you give up.
what it means: a living sacrifice is a whole life, body and ordinary days, offered in thanks for God's mercies, and transformed by the renewing of the mind.
what a scholar hears: logikē latreia can mean reasonable, rational or spiritual worship, and the passive metamorphousthe matches Mark 9:2, where Jesus was transfigured.
